extracted.intended_audience: employers, immigration attorneys, HR professionals, OFLC/ETA staff, and stakeholders responding to or implementing prevailing wage / PERM / LCA regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for determining and using prevailing wages for labor certification (PERM) and LCA processes, including required data sources, computation of four wage levels, NPC/OFLC procedures, acceptable employer surveys, and related administrative-review and impact-assessment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources for prevailing wage
rubrics_metrics.description: If the job opportunity is not covered by a CBA, the prevailing wage shall be based on the wages of workers similarly employed as determined by the wage component of the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics Survey (OEWS) in accordance with 20 CFR 656.40(b)(2)(i); a current wage as determined in the area under the Davis-Bacon Act; the McNamara-O'Hara Service Contract Act; an independent authoritative source; or another legitimate source of wage data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prevailing wage rate shall be based on the best information available. The rule lists permissible prevailing wage sources (OEWS, Davis-Bacon, SCA, independent authoritative sources, other legitimate sources) and identifies when each may be used (see paragraphs (a)(2)(ii)(A)-(C) and §656.40(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OFLC NPC prevailing wage determinations (PWDs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPC shall receive and process prevailing wage determination requests in accordance with these regulations and Department guidance. Upon receipt of a written request for a PWD, the NPC will determine whether the occupation is covered by a collective bargaining agreement and, if not, determine the wages of workers similarly employed using the wage component of the BLS OEWS and selecting an appropriate wage level in accordance with 20 CFR 656.40(b)(2)(i), unless the employer provides an acceptable survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NPC determinations follow 20 CFR 656.40 and ETA administrative guidance. NPC shall specify the validity period of the PWD (not less than 90 days and not more than 1 year). If employer-provided acceptable surveys supply mean or median, NPC will use those values as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic mean vs. median rule for prevailing wages
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employer uses an independent authoritative source or other legitimate source of wage data, the prevailing wage shall be the arithmetic mean of the wages of workers similarly employed, except that the prevailing wage shall be the median when provided by specified paragraphs. If an acceptable employer-provided wage survey provides an arithmetic mean then that wage shall be the prevailing wage; if an acceptable employer-provided wage survey provides a median and does not provide an arithmetic mean, the median shall be the prevailing wage applicable to the employer's job opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers relying on surveys must note whether the survey reports a mean or median; use mean when available, use median only if mean not provided and median is the only available central tendency measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer reliance on alternate sources pending NPC PWD
rubrics_metrics.description: If the employer is unable to wait for the NPC to produce the requested prevailing wage, the employer may rely on other legitimate sources of available wage information as set forth in paragraphs (a)(2)(ii)(B) and (C). If the employer later discovers, upon receipt of the PWD from the NPC, that the information relied upon produced a wage below the final PWD and the employer was not paying the NPC-determined wage, no wage violation will be found if the employer retroactively compensates the H-1B nonimmigrant(s) for the difference between the wage paid and the prevailing wage, within 30 days of the employer's receipt of the PWD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits temporary reliance on alternative data but conditions immunity from violation on prompt (within 30 days) retroactive payment of any difference after NPC PWD issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer application process for PWDs
rubrics_metrics.description: The employer must request a PWD from the NPC, on a form or in a manner prescribed by OFLC. The NPC shall receive and process prevailing wage determination requests in accordance with these regulations and Department guidance. Unless the employer chooses to appeal the center's PWD under §656.41(a), it files the Application for Permanent Employment Certification either electronically or by mail with the NPC and maintains the PWD in its files. The determination shall be submitted to the Certifying Officer (CO), if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must use OFLC-prescribed forms/methods, maintain PWD documentation, and may appeal under §656.41(a) if desired. NPC processing and retention rules govern administrative compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-level wage structure (Level I–IV) and computation
rubrics_metrics.description: The BLS shall provide OEWS wage data computed and assigned at levels set commensurate with education, experience, and level of supervision. The OFLC Administrator will provide prevailing wages at four levels: Level I = 34th percentile; Level II = Level I + (Level IV - Level I)/3; Level III = Level IV - (Level IV - Level I)/3; Level IV = 88th percentile, assigned for the most specific occupation and geographic area available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows INA §212(p)(4) and 20 CFR methodology. The four levels are tied to education/experience/supervision and are computed from OEWS distributions per the formulas provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level IV fallback computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Level IV Wage cannot be computed due to wage values exceeding the uppermost interval of the OEWS wage interval methodology, the OFLC Administrator shall determine the Level IV Wage using the current hourly wage rate applicable to the highest OEWS wage interval for the specific occupation and geographic area, or the arithmetic mean of the wages of all workers for the most specific occupation and geographic area available, whichever is highest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a specific fallback method where OEWS percentile cannot be directly calculated because of top-coded intervals; choose the higher of top-interval wage rate or arithmetic mean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual publication of prevailing wage levels
rubrics_metrics.description: The OFLC Administrator will publish, at least once in each calendar year, on a date to be determined by the OFLC Administrator, the prevailing wage levels under paragraph (b)(2)(i) of this section as a notice posted on the OFLC website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFLC must make the computed Level I–IV wages publicly available at least annually via website notice so employers and practitioners can reference official published levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable employer-provided survey rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the employer provides a survey acceptable under paragraph (g) of this section, the prevailing wage for labor certification purposes shall be the arithmetic mean of the wages of workers similarly employed in the area of intended employment. If an otherwise acceptable survey provides a median and does not provide an arithmetic mean, the prevailing wage applicable to the employer's job opportunity shall be the median of the wages of workers similarly employed in the area of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer surveys may be used when they meet the acceptability criteria in paragraph (g); when acceptable they determine prevailing wage by the survey's arithmetic mean or, lacking that, its median.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity period of NPC PWDs
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPC shall specify the validity period of the PWD, which in no event shall be for less than 90 days or more than 1 year from the date of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWDs cannot be issued with validity shorter than 90 days or longer than one year; employers must rely on a PWD within that window or obtain a new determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevailing wage must be based on 'best information available'
rubrics_metrics.description: The prevailing wage rate shall be based on the best information available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisionmakers (NPC, OFLC) and employers should choose the most reliable current wage data source practicable when determining the prevailing wage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective bargaining agreement (CBA) check in PWDs
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a written request for a PWD, the NPC will determine whether the occupation is covered by a collective bargaining agreement which was negotiated at arm's length, and, if not, determine the wages of workers similarly employed using OEWS or acceptable survey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide CBA covers the job opportunity, the CBA may govern wages instead of OEWS/survey-derived wages; NPC must make this determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: E.O. 12988 (Civil Justice Reform) drafting/clarity standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3(a) requires agencies to: (1) eliminate drafting errors and ambiguity, (2) write regulations to minimize litigation, (3) provide a clear legal standard for affected conduct rather than a general standard, and (4) promote simplification and burden reduction. Section 3(b) requires agencies to: (1) clearly specify the preemptive effect, if any, (2) clearly specify any effect on existing Federal law or regulation, (3) provide a clear legal standard for affected conduct while promoting simplification and burden reduction, (4) specify the retroactive effect, if any, (5) adequately define key terms, and (6) address other important issues affecting clarity and general draftsmanship under any guidelines issued by the Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must review regulations for adherence to these requirements and document whether standards are met or it is unreasonable to meet them. The Department concluded this NPRM meets relevant standards to extent permitted by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 13132 requires agencies to examine the constitutional and statutory authority supporting any action that would limit the policymaking discretion of the States and to assess necessity for such actions, and to have an accountable process to ensure meaningful and timely input by State and local officials when regulatory policies have federalism implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must assess whether rule has substantial direct effects on States or distribution of power and responsibilities among levels of government. The Department determined this NPRM would not have such substantial direct effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13175 (Tribal consultation) review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: E.O. 13175 requires agencies to consult and coordinate with Indian tribal governments when a rule has tribal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must determine whether a rule has tribal implications (effects on tribes or distribution of power); the Department determined this proposed rule does not have tribal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: UMRA requires Federal agencies to assess a regulation's effects on state, local, and tribal governments, as well as on the private sector, and to prepare a written statement if a rule includes a Federal mandate that may result in $100 million or more expenditure in any one year by governments or the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must analyze and state whether the rule contains intergovernmental mandates or will require expenditures of $100M+; the Department determined this rule does not contain an intergovernmental mandate nor exceed the $100M threshold, but UMRA analytical requirements apply with respect to private sector effects (see section III.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) / OMB control number criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of information is subject to PRA review and OMB approval if it displays a currently valid OMB control number (44 U.S.C. 3512). The Department determined that the changes proposed to the computation of the prevailing wage levels do not require a collection of information subject to OMB approval under the PRA, or affect any existing collections of information covered under certain OMB control numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any regulatory change that creates or modifies an information collection must be evaluated for PRA/O MB approval; this NPRM asserts no new collections are required and no changes sought to listed control numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasury and General Government Appropriations Act (family policymaking) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 654 requires agencies to issue a Family Policymaking Assessment for any rule that may affect family well-being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must assess whether the rule affects the autonomy or integrity of the family; the Department concluded no Family Policymaking Assessment was necessary for this NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information quality review under Treasury and General Government Appropriations Act, 2001
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 515 provides for agency review of most disseminations of information to the public under information quality guidelines established by each agency pursuant to OMB guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must review the NPRM under applicable OMB information quality guidelines; the Department concluded the NPRM is consistent with applicable policies in those guidelines.
